commissioned_scope: All original RG-24 commissioned A/B subjects, full Mackey theorem, uniqueness, abelian-normal semidirect-product corollary and examples retained; no new pair.

lem-spectral-measure-of-a-representation.interface: Assume AC, and let $N$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff abelian group, $\pi:N\to U(\mathcal H)$ a strongly continuous unitary representation on a separable Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, and $K$ a second-countable locally compact group acting continuously on $N$ by automorphisms $\alpha_k$, with dual action $k\cdot\chi=\chi\circ\alpha_k^{-1}$ on $\widehat N$. If $\tau:K\to U(\mathcal H)$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation with $\tau(k)\pi(n)\tau(k)^{-1}=\pi(\alpha_k(n))$, then there is a unique regular projection-valued measure $P$ on $\widehat N$ with $$\pi(n)=\int_{\widehat N}\chi(n)\,dP(\chi)\qquad(n\in N),\qquad \tau(k)P(E)\tau(k)^{-1}=P(k\cdot E)$$ for every Borel $E\subseteq\widehat N$. If in addition the representation $n\mapsto\pi(n)$, $k\mapsto\tau(k)$ of $N\rtimes K$ is irreducible, then the measure class of $P$ is ergodic for the action of $K$ on $\widehat N$: every Borel $E$ with $P(E)$ invariant under $\tau$ satisfies $P(E)=0$ or $P(E)=I$.
lem-spectral-measure-of-a-representation.strategy:
For $f\in L^1(N)$ define $\pi(f)\xi=\int f(n)\pi(n)\xi dn$. Bochner integrability and Fubini prove a bounded star-homomorphism, and an approximate identity supported in neighborhoods of e gives $\pi(f_i)\xi\to\xi$ by strong continuity. Let A be the norm closure of its image. Nonunital Gelfand-Naimark gives $\|\pi(f)\|=\sup_{y\in\Delta(A)}|y(\pi(f))|$. Each composition $y\circ\pi$ is nonzero because the image is dense and y is nonzero, hence the proved local L1-character lemma identifies it with integration against a character of N. Therefore $\|\pi(f)\|\le\|\widehat f\|_\infty$. The dense-C0 Fourier lemma now extends $\widehat f\mapsto\pi(f)$ uniquely to a nondegenerate star representation of $C_0(\widehat N)$; no injectivity of the Fourier transform is needed because the norm bound makes the map well-defined. The local C0-PVM lemma gives the unique regular PVM P with $\pi(f)=\int\widehat f dP$.
The operators $R(n)=\int\chi(n)dP(\chi)$ form a strongly continuous unitary representation: multiplication of characters gives the group law and scalar dominated convergence gives strong continuity through $\|(R(n)-R(n_0))\xi\|^2=\int|\chi(n)-\chi(n_0)|^2dP_\xi$. Second countability allows sequences here. Fubini on each finite scalar PVM measure shows that the L1 averages of R and pi agree. Their continuous matrix coefficients therefore agree at each n: otherwise a compactly supported nonnegative test function in a neighborhood where their difference has a fixed nonzero real part would distinguish the averages. Thus $\pi(n)=R(n)$. Any other regular PVM with this formula gives the same Fourier-transform integrals by Fubini and then the same C0 representation by density, so is P. Conjugating by tau(k) and applying the dual change of variables gives a second regular PVM for the conjugated representation; uniqueness yields $\tau(k)P(E)\tau(k)^{-1}=P(kE)$. Finally each such invariant P(E) commutes with pi(N) by the PVM integral and with tau(K) by hypothesis, so its range and orthogonal complement are invariant under the irreducible semidirect-product representation and P(E) is 0 or I. All spectral and character-space inputs now have proved suppliers.

lem-borel-cocycle-fields-for-imprimitivi.interface: Assume AC. Let $(U,P)$ be a transitive system of imprimitivity on $G/H$ and fix a normalization $W:H_0\to L^2(G/H,\mu;K)$ with $WP(E)W^{-1}=M_{\mathbf 1_E}$, $G$ second countable locally compact, $H$ closed, $K$ separable, $\mu$ quasi-invariant. For $g\in G$ let $V_g$ be the canonical translation operator $(V_gf)(x)=[d((L_g)_*\mu)/d\mu(x)]^{1/2}f(g^{-1}x)$ and put $W_g=V_g^{-1}WU_gW^{-1}$. Then $W_g$ commutes with all multiplications and is therefore multiplication by an essentially bounded measurable operator field $x\mapsto\varphi_g(x)\in\mathcal B(K)$; the field may be chosen so that $(g,x)\mapsto\langle\varphi_g(x)\xi,\eta\rangle$ is Borel on $G\times G/H$ for $\xi,\eta$ in a fixed dense countable subset of $K$ and so that $\varphi_g(x)$ is unitary for almost every $x$ and every $g$, with the cocycle identity $$\varphi_{g_1g_2}(x)=\varphi_{g_1}(g_2x)\,\varphi_{g_2}(x)$$ holding for every $g_1,g_2$ and almost every $x$.
lem-borel-cocycle-fields-for-imprimitivi.strategy:
Let $T_g=WU_gW^{-1}$ and let $V_g$ be the scalar induced translations. The published induction results give strongly continuous V; for an equivalent finite measure this follows by conjugating with the square root of the measure density. Covariance gives $W_g=V_g^{-1}T_g$ in the diagonal commutant, and the published decomposable-commutant theorem gives its a.e. unitary fibre class. To select jointly Borel representatives explicitly, replace the base measure by an equivalent probability and fix an orthonormal basis $(e_j)$ of K. The L2-valued maps $g\mapsto W_g(1e_j)$ are continuous. For each j choose a countable dense set of Borel simple L2 functions; at stage n take the least function within $2^{-n}$ of $W_g(1e_j)$. The chosen index is Borel in g. Summability of the L2 errors, hence of the L1 errors on the probability base, makes the Borel approximants converge pointwise almost everywhere for every fixed g. Their limit columns give jointly Borel coefficients of a field $\varphi_g$ representing Wg. On the Borel set where the countably many columns fail the unitary equations put the field equal to I; that set is null in x for each g. This supplies unitary values everywhere and the required joint Borel field. In the original measure the same representatives work by equivalence. The zero fibre is trivial.
Expanding $W_{g_1g_2}=V_{g_2}^{-1}W_{g_1}V_{g_2}W_{g_2}$ gives $\varphi_{g_1g_2}(x)=\varphi_{g_1}(g_2x)\varphi_{g_2}(x)$ for each pair and almost every x, by uniqueness of decomposable fields. Strong continuity of Wg implies continuity in local measure of its columns (test the constant basis sections on finite-measure pieces), so $g\mapsto\varphi_g$ has the continuity required by Haar regularization. The associated action is $T_gf(x)=D_g(x)^{1/2}\varphi_g(g^{-1}x)f(g^{-1}x)$: the field is evaluated at the source variable. Neither the joint representative construction nor the pairwise a.e. law licenses evaluation at eH; the Haar regularization supplier supplies that separate step.

lem-the-stabilizer-action-on-an-imprimit.interface: Assume AC and let $(U,P)$ be a transitive system on $G/H$ on a separable Hilbert space, with multiplicity-normalized model and source-variable cocycle fields $\varphi_g$ as above. Fix a Borel section $s$ with $s(eH)=e$. There exist a Borel unitary field $B_x$ and a strongly continuous unitary representation $\sigma:H\to U(K)$, unique up to unitary equivalence, such that for every g and almost every x, $\varphi_g(x)=B_{gx}\sigma(h(g,x))B_x^{-1}$, where $h(g,x)=s(gx)^{-1}gs(x)$. The representatives can be replaced by this strict formula on all pairs and normalized with $B_{eH}=I$, so that $\sigma(h)=\varphi_h(eH)$ and $B_x=\varphi_{s(x)}(eH)$. Changes of fields or section give equivalent $\sigma$. If H=G one recovers the original representation; if H is trivial the recovered representation is trivial.
lem-the-stabilizer-action-on-an-imprimit.strategy: Apply Haar regularization to the jointly Borel source cocycle: the cocycle lemma supplies continuity in local measure, and the Haar-lift/descent and regularization lemmas prove every measurable step. They produce B and a strongly continuous sigma with the displayed factorization, without evaluating an a.e. class at eH. Set $s(eH)=e$ by a Borel single-point modification. If the base point is null, set $B_{eH}=I$; for fixed g this modifies the factorization only on $\{eH,g^{-1}eH\}$, both null. If it is an atom, conjugate the entire factorization by $B_{eH}$ to normalize that value. Replace the fields by the strict Borel formula and now, only now, evaluate it at eH to obtain $\varphi_h(eH)=\sigma(h)$ and $\varphi_{s(x)}(eH)=B_x$. The strict section identity verifies the cocycle law everywhere. Uniqueness under a.e. representative or gauge changes is the Haar-Fubini uniqueness argument in the regularization lemma; a change of section changes B by its corresponding sigma factor and leaves the equivalence class fixed. The one-point and trivial-stabilizer cases follow directly from the factorization.

lem-characters-of-l1-of-an-abelian-lch-g.interface: Assume AC. For a second-countable LCH abelian group $N$ with Haar measure, every nonzero complex-linear multiplicative functional $\lambda$ on $L^1(N)$ is uniquely $\lambda(f)=\int_N f(n)\chi(n)\,dn$ for a continuous unitary character $\chi$. This bijection from $\widehat N$ with its compact-open topology to the character space with its pointwise-evaluation topology is a homeomorphism. No Pontryagin duality or Fourier inversion theorem is assumed.
lem-characters-of-l1-of-an-abelian-lch-g.strategy:
Extend $\lambda$ to the sum-norm unitization by $(z,f)\mapsto z+\lambda(f)$; the published automatic-continuity theorem gives $|\lambda(f)|\le\|f\|_1$. Choose $k\in L^1(N)$ with $\lambda(k)\ne0$ and set $\chi(n)=\lambda(L_nk)/\lambda(k)$. The identity $(L_nf)*k=f*(L_nk)$ and multiplicativity show $\lambda(L_nf)=\chi(n)\lambda(f)$ for every $f$. Applying this twice to $L_mk$ gives $\chi(nm)=\chi(n)\chi(m)$; L1 translation continuity gives continuity, and $|\chi(n)|\le\|k\|_1/|\lambda(k)|$ for all $n$. The powers of $n$ and $n^{-1}$ force $|\chi(n)|=1$. As a Bochner L1 integral, $f*k=\int f(n)L_nk\,dn$: strong measurability follows from continuous translation and second countability, absolute norm integrability is $\|f\|_1\|k\|_1$, and Fubini identifies the integral with convolution. Applying $\lambda$ and dividing by $\lambda(k)$ gives the classification formula. Conversely that formula is nonzero (choose a nonnegative compactly supported bump times $\overline\chi$), bounded, and multiplicative by Fubini. Distinct continuous characters give distinct functionals by such bumps near a point where they differ.
For topology, compact-open convergence gives convergence of every integral by first making the L1 tail outside a compact set small. Conversely if $\lambda_i\to\lambda$ pointwise, fix the same $k$ with $\lambda(k)\ne0$. The set $\{L_nk:n\in C\}$ is norm compact for each compact $C\subset N$; norm bounds $\|\lambda_i\|\le1$ and a finite norm-net upgrade pointwise convergence on this set to uniform convergence. The denominators $\lambda_i(k)$ tend to a nonzero number, so the displayed ratio gives uniform convergence of $\chi_i$ on $C$. This argument works with nets and proves the asserted homeomorphism.

lem-lca-fourier-transforms-form-a-dense-.interface: Assume AC and let $N$ be a second-countable LCH abelian group. With $\widehat f(\chi)=\int f(n)\chi(n)dn$, each $f\in L^1(N)$ has $\widehat f\in C_0(\widehat N)$, and the functions $\widehat f$ form a self-adjoint separating nowhere-vanishing algebra whose uniform closure is $C_0(\widehat N)$. No injectivity or inversion claim is needed.
lem-lca-fourier-transforms-form-a-dense-.strategy: The character space of the sum-norm unitization of L1 is a closed subset of its weak-star compact dual unit ball: the equations $\psi(1)=1$ and $\psi(ab)=\psi(a)\psi(b)$ are closed. Every such character either restricts nontrivially to L1 or is $q(z,f)=z$; therefore the space is $\widehat N\cup\{q\}$ by the preceding lemma, with $\widehat N$ open (it is the union of sets $\psi(f)\ne0$). The continuous evaluation $\psi\mapsto\psi(f)$ vanishes at $q$, so its $\epsilon$-superlevel sets are compact and contained in $\widehat N$. This proves $\widehat f\in C_0$ including the discrete case, where $q$ is isolated. Fubini and conjugate-reflection give $\widehat{f*k}=\widehat f\widehat k$ and $\widehat{f^*}=\overline{\widehat f}$. Character classification gives separation; a bump times $\overline\chi$ gives nonvanishing at each $\chi$. On this compact character space adjoin constants and apply the published compact complex Stone-Weierstrass theorem: the algebra separates also $q$ from every other character. To approximate a continuous function vanishing at $q$, subtract from each approximant its value at $q$; the error at most doubles and the resulting approximants are Fourier transforms. Restriction gives the C0 density claim.

lem-nondegenerate-czero-representations-.interface: Assume AC. Let $X$ be LCH and $T:C_0(X)\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ a nondegenerate star representation. Then a unique regular PVM $P$ on $X$ with $P(X)=I$ satisfies $T(f)=\int_X f\,dP$ for every $f\in C_0(X)$. The zero Hilbert space has the zero PVM.
lem-nondegenerate-czero-representations-.strategy: For nonzero $\mathcal H$, use $X^+=X\cup\{\infty\}$ (with an isolated extra point if $X$ is compact) and extend $T$ unitaly by $T^+(f+c)=T(f)+cI$. The published compact-space regular-PVM theorem gives $E$ on $X^+$. Each $T(f)E(\{\infty\})$ is zero because $f(\infty)=0$; nondegeneracy, i.e. density of $T(C_0(X))\mathcal H$, therefore forces $E(\{\infty\})=0$. Restrict $E$ to $X$; finite scalar measures retain regularity on the open subspace and have total mass $\|\xi\|^2$. Conversely any such PVM extends by zero at infinity, so uniqueness follows from the compact theorem. Treat $\mathcal H=0$ directly.

lem-haar-lifts-and-borel-descent-on-a-ho.interface: Assume AC. Let $G$ be second-countable LCH, $H$ closed, $q:G\to G/H$, and $s$ a Borel section. Every nonzero sigma-finite quasi-invariant Borel measure $\mu$ on $G/H$ is equivalent to a rho-derived quotient measure. The coordinates $(x,h)\mapsto s(x)h$ carry the product quotient/Haar measure class to the Haar measure class on $G$. In particular $\mu(E)=0$ iff $q^{-1}(E)$ is Haar null. If a Borel map $F:G/H\times H\to U(K)$ for separable $K$ satisfies $F(x,hk)=F(x,h)$ for every $k$ and almost every $(x,h)$, then $F(x,h)=B(x)$ almost everywhere for a Borel $B:G/H\to U(K)$.
lem-haar-lifts-and-borel-descent-on-a-ho.strategy:
The section is a Borel bijection in the displayed coordinates with inverse $t\mapsto(q(t),s(q(t))^{-1}t)$. Extend the published Weil equality from Cc to nonnegative Borel functions by equality of sigma-finite measures on the second-countable LCH space G (Cc cutoffs and monotone-class approximation suffice). Its left measure is $ho(t)dt$, equivalent to Haar, and its right measure is the pushforward of $d\mu_ho(x)dh$, proving the coordinate/null-class assertion. To prove the assertion for an arbitrary quasi-invariant $\mu$, replace it by an equivalent probability and choose a probability $
u=w(g)dg$ with $w>0$ Haar-a.e. For Borel E set $\overline\mu(E)=\int\mu(g^{-1}E)d
u(g)$. Each translate is equivalent to $\mu$, so Tonelli gives $\overline\mu\sim\mu$: positivity for positive E holds for every g. For each fixed x, the map $g\mapsto gx$ is $q$ after a right Haar translation; thus the inner measure $
u\{g:gx\in E\}$ is zero iff $\mu_ho(E)=0$, and is positive otherwise. Another application of Tonelli gives $\overline\mu\sim\mu_ho$, as required.
For descent, the invariance holds almost everywhere in $(x,h,k)$ by Tonelli, after taking countably many matrix coefficients. For almost every x, change variables $(h,k)\mapsto(h,hk)$, which preserves Haar product null sets, to conclude $F(x,h_1)=F(x,h_2)$ for almost all pairs. Thus $F(x,\cdot)$ is almost everywhere constant. Integrate its matrix coefficients against a fixed strictly positive probability density on H to obtain the constant's coefficients Borelly; the constants are unitary for almost every x. The set of coefficient matrices representing a unitary is Borel (the countable orthonormal-basis isometry and surjectivity equations), so put B=I on the exceptional Borel set. This gives the claimed Borel descent. No evaluation on a prescribed null coset is used.

lem-haar-regularization-of-transitive-un.interface: Assume AC. Let $G,H,\mu,s$ be as in the Haar-lift lemma, $K$ separable, and $c:G\times G/H\to U(K)$ Borel with $c(g_1g_2,x)=c(g_1,g_2x)c(g_2,x)$ for each pair and almost every x. Suppose $g\mapsto c(g,\cdot)$ is continuous in local convergence in measure in the strong topology of $U(K)$. Then there exist a strongly continuous unitary representation $\sigma:H\to U(K)$ and a Borel $B:G/H\to U(K)$ with $c(g,x)=B(gx)\sigma(s(gx)^{-1}gs(x))B(x)^{-1}$ for every g and almost every x. This formula gives a strict Borel cocycle on all of $G\times G/H$. The representation $\sigma$ is unique up to unitary equivalence under Borel changes of fibre gauge.
lem-haar-regularization-of-transitive-un.strategy:
Use the Haar null-class lemma to lift the pairwise a.e. identity to G, and Tonelli to obtain it for Haar-almost all triples of group variables. Set $C(u,v)=c(uv^{-1},q(v))$. The coordinate change $(u,v,w)\leftrightarrow(uv^{-1},vw^{-1},w)$ preserves product Haar null classes, by Haar translations and their positive modular factors. The cocycle law becomes $C(u,v)C(v,w)=C(u,w)$ a.e. Select $w_0$ by Fubini so this holds a.e. in $(u,v)$ and put $b(u)=C(u,w_0)$. Then $C(u,v)=b(u)b(v)^{-1}$ almost everywhere, or $c(g,q(t))=b(gt)b(t)^{-1}$ for almost all $(g,t)$. Extend this equality to each fixed g in local convergence in measure: the left side is continuous by hypothesis and pullback (on each finite Haar set its quotient image measure is absolutely continuous to $\mu$); the right side is continuous because translations of a Borel U(K)-valued b are continuous in local measure. For the latter claim, use a countable orthonormal basis, approximate each bounded coefficient or vector $b(t)e_j$ on compact sets by simple functions and then continuous compactly supported functions, use the published L2 translation continuity, and bound the error uniformly for translations in a compact neighborhood by the modular change-of-variable factors. This proves the stated continuity in a countable metric for the strong topology. An a.e. equality between continuous maps on G is everywhere equality, since Haar has full support.
For fixed h in H define $A_h(t)=b(t)^{-1}b(th)$. The equality just proved and $q(th)=q(t)$ imply $A_h(gt)=A_h(t)$ for each g and Haar-a.e. t. Tonelli and the change $(g,t)\mapsto(gt,t)$ show $A_h$ is a.e. a constant unitary $\sigma(h)$. Constants satisfy $\sigma(hk)=\sigma(h)\sigma(k)$ by applying $b(th)=b(t)\sigma(h)$ twice and using nonsingularity of right translations. Integrating the coefficients of $A_h$ against a positive probability density on G makes h\mapsto\sigma(h) Borel; the published Borel-homomorphism Steinhaus-Pettis lemma yields strong continuity, since U(K) is second countable in the strong topology. In section coordinates $F(x,r)=b(s(x)r)\sigma(r)^{-1}$ satisfies $F(x,rh)=F(x,r)$ for each h and almost all $(x,r)$, by the Haar-lift lemma. Its descent supplies B with $b(t)=B(q(t))\sigma(s(q(t))^{-1}t)$ Haar-a.e. For every fixed g, substitute this at t and gt in the preceding identity; the right-H factors cancel, giving the claimed formula on the quotient a.e. Its all-point extension is a cocycle by the exact section identity, without imposing values at a null base point.
For uniqueness, if $(B_i,\sigma_i)$ give the same c, set $b_i(t)=B_i(q(t))\sigma_i(s(q(t))^{-1}t)$. Then $b_2(gt)^{-1}b_1(gt)=b_2(t)^{-1}b_1(t)$ for each g and almost every t. The same Haar-Fubini argument makes this a constant unitary T. Right-H covariance now gives $\sigma_2(h)T=T\sigma_1(h)$ for every h. A Borel fibre gauge multiplies both lifted trivializations on the left and therefore has the same conclusion. This also proves uniqueness for intertwiners between separable fibres of equal dimension.

lem-borel-cross-sections-for-closed-subg.interface: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff topological group, $H\le G$ a closed subgroup, and $q:G\to G/H$ the quotient map. Then there is a Borel cross-section $s:G/H\to G$ with $q\circ s=\mathrm{id}_{G/H}$, and for every $g\in G$ there is a unique $h(g,\cdot)\in H$ with $g\,s(x)=s(gx)\,h(g,x)$, where $x\in G/H$; the map $(g,x)\mapsto h(g,x)$ is Borel into $H$. Consequently the map $G\to G/H\times H$, $g\mapsto(q(g),s(q(g))^{-1}g)$, is a Borel isomorphism onto $G/H\times H$, and the quasi-invariant measure class on $G/H$ may be transported to a sigma-finite measure on $G$ along $s$.
lem-borel-cross-sections-for-closed-subg.strategy: The quotient map is open because $q^{-1}(q(O))=OH$ is open for open O. Choose a compatible metric on G and a countable base of relatively compact open sets. For each n keep those base sets of diameter at most $2^{-n}$; this is still a base. For x choose the least such set $O_1$ with $x\in q(O_1)$; recursively choose the least $O_{n+1}$ with $\overline{O_{n+1}}\subset O_n$ and $x\in q(O_{n+1})$. Such a choice exists since the closed fibre meets O_n and local compactness permits a smaller base neighborhood around a point of that intersection. Each selected index is Borel in x, because q of a base set is open and containment of closures is a fixed relation between the countably many base indices. The nested compact closures lie in $\overline O_1$ and have diameter tending to zero, so their intersection is one point s(x). Since the closed fibre meets every O_n, this point lies in the fibre. Fix one point in each base set; the selected points are Borel functions of x and converge to s(x), proving Borelness. The formula $h(g,x)=s(gx)^{-1}gs(x)$ proves existence, uniqueness and Borelness of the section cocycle. The coordinates $(x,h)\mapsto s(x)h$ and $g\mapsto(q(g),s(q(g))^{-1}g)$ are mutually inverse Borel maps onto all of $G/H\times H$. Pushing a sigma-finite quotient measure along the injective section gives a sigma-finite Borel measure on its Borel image; this is only a section-supported measure, while Haar lifting is supplied by the separate Weil lemma.

lem-a-transitive-quasi-invariant-borel-g.interface: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff topological group, $H\le G$ a closed subgroup, and $\mu$ a nonzero quasi-invariant Radon measure on $G/H$. If $E\subseteq G/H$ is Borel with $\mu(E\,\triangle\,gE)=0$ for every $g\in G$, then $\mu(E)=0$ or $\mu((G/H)\setminus E)=0$. Equivalently, any transitive system of imprimitivity on $G/H$ whose measure class is the quasi-invariant class is ergodic.
lem-a-transitive-quasi-invariant-borel-g.strategy: By the Haar-lift lemma the quotient measure class is the Haar quotient class. Lift $\mathbf1_E$ to $f(t)=\mathbf1_E(q(t))$. The hypothesis says $f(gt)=f(t)$ Haar-a.e. t for every g. Tonelli and the null-class-preserving change $(g,t)\mapsto(gt,t)$ yield $f(u)=f(t)$ for almost all pairs (u,t). A Fubini section therefore makes f a.e. a constant, necessarily 0 or 1. By the quotient null-class equivalence this means E is null or conull. This avoids the unsupported assertion that countably many translates of an arbitrary positive-measure compact set cover G/H.

lem-steinhaus-and-pettis-for-second-coun.interface: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff topological group with left Haar measure $\mu$. (i) If $A\subseteq G$ is Borel with $0<\mu(A)<\infty$, then $AA^{-1}$ contains an open neighborhood of the identity. (ii) If $T$ is a second-countable topological group and $\varphi:G\to T$ is a Borel-measurable group homomorphism, then $\varphi$ is continuous. In particular, a Borel homomorphism from $H$ into the unitary group $U(K)$ of a separable Hilbert space, with the strong operator topology, is strongly continuous.
lem-steinhaus-and-pettis-for-second-coun.strategy: For (i), L2 translation continuity applied to $\mathbf1_A$ makes $g\mapsto\langle L_g\mathbf1_A,\mathbf1_A\rangle=\mu(gA\cap A)$ continuous, with value $\mu(A)>0$ at e. Therefore $gA\cap A\ne\varnothing$ in an identity neighborhood, so $g\in AA^{-1}$. For (ii), take a symmetric identity neighborhood V of T with $V^2\subset U$. The subspace $\varphi(G)$ is second countable and hence Lindelof, so its cover by $\varphi(g)V\cap\varphi(G)$ has a countable subcover with centers $\varphi(g_n)$ actually in the image. If $\varphi^{-1}(V)$ were null then the sets $g_n\varphi^{-1}(V)$ would cover G by null sets, contradicting positivity of Haar. Thus the preimage has positive measure; intersect it with a compact exhaustion to obtain a positive finite-measure Borel subset A. By (i), an identity neighborhood lies in $AA^{-1}\subset\varphi^{-1}(V^2)\subset\varphi^{-1}(U)$, proving continuity at e and hence everywhere. For separable K the strong unitary topology is metrized by the actions on a countable orthonormal basis; U(K) embeds in the countable product of the separable metric spaces K, so it is second countable.

lem-ergodic-imprimitivity-systems-with-r.interface: Assume AC. Let $(U,P)$ be an ergodic system of imprimitivity for a Borel action of a group $G$ on a standard Borel space $X$, acting on a nonzero separable Hilbert space, and suppose the orbit equivalence relation of the action is **regular**: there is a countable family $E_1,E_2,\dots$ of $G$-invariant Borel subsets of $X$ such that every orbit is the intersection of the sets $E_n$ that contain it. Then there is an orbit $C\subseteq X$ with $P(X\setminus C)=0$.
lem-ergodic-imprimitivity-systems-with-r.strategy: Ergodicity makes each invariant projection $P(E_n)$ either zero or I. Put $F_n=E_n$ in the latter case and $F_n=X\setminus E_n$ in the former. Then $P(F_n)=I$ for every n. The complements have zero scalar measure for every vector; countable additivity implies $P(C)=I$ for $C=\bigcap_nF_n$. Since the Hilbert space is nonzero, C is nonempty. Pick x in C. Its orbit lies in C because the F_n are invariant; conversely any y in C belongs to every E_n containing x, so the regularity hypothesis puts y in the orbit of x. Thus C is exactly one orbit and is Borel as the countable intersection. No assertion that the countable Boolean algebra has countably many nonempty atoms is needed; its signature classes may be uncountable.

def-transformation-algebra-of-a-g-space.interface: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological group acting continuously on a locally compact Hausdorff space $X$, with left Haar measure $dg$ and modular function $\Delta_G$. The **transformation algebra** of the action is the complex vector space $C_c(G\times X)$ of continuous complex functions with compact support, equipped with the twisted convolution $$(f_1*f_2)(g,x)=\int_G f_1(h,x)\,f_2(h^{-1}g,h^{-1}x)\,dh$$ and the involution $f^*(g,x)=\Delta_G(g)^{-1}\overline{f(g^{-1},g^{-1}x)}$. The formulas define a complex associative algebra with involution; when the action is trivial the formula is convolution in the group variable with pointwise multiplication in the base variable.
def-transformation-algebra-of-a-g-space.strategy: Use the target-variable convention in the statement. The first factor restricts h to a compact group set and x to a compact base set; the second restricts $h^{-1}g$ to a compact group set. Thus convolution has compact support inside the product of the two group projections and the first base projection. Near any (g,x), uniform continuity on compact parameter sets and a common compact h-support justify continuity of the integral. Both associative expansions are the double integral of $f_1(h,x)f_2(r,h^{-1}x)f_3(r^{-1}h^{-1}g,r^{-1}h^{-1}x)$ after the left-Haar substitution k=hr, proving associativity. For the involution, double application gives f by $\Delta(g^{-1})=\Delta(g)^{-1}$; expanding $f_2^**f_1^*$ combines the modular factors into $\Delta(g)^{-1}$, and substituting r=gh gives exactly $(f_1*f_2)^*(g,x)$. The support transforms by the continuous map $(g,x)\mapsto(g^{-1},g^{-1}x)$, so remains compact. These computations prove the algebra and star identities rather than importing them from a source. AC is inherited through the published compactly supported kernel theorem used to commute the Radon integrals in the associativity argument; no additional independent choice step is claimed.

lem-a-system-of-imprimitivity-gives-a-re.interface: Assume AC. Let $(U,P)$ be a system of imprimitivity on a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff $G$-space $X$ with continuous action, as required by the transformation-algebra definition. For $f\in C_c(G\times X)$ define $\pi(f)$ by the scalar pairing $$\langle\pi(f)\xi,\eta\rangle=\int_G\int_X f(g,x)\,d\langle P(x)\,U_g\xi,\eta\rangle\,dg\qquad(\xi,\eta\in H).$$ Then $\pi(f)$ is a bounded operator, $\|\pi(f)\|\le\int_G\|f(g,\cdot)\|_\infty\,dg$, the map $f\mapsto\pi(f)$ is a $*$-representation of the transformation algebra $C_c(G\times X)$, and it is nondegenerate: the closed span of $\pi(C_c(G\times X))H$ is $H$.
lem-a-system-of-imprimitivity-gives-a-re.strategy: For fixed g, let $M_{f(g,\cdot)}=\int f(g,x)dP(x)$. For each vector, $g\mapsto M_{f(g,\cdot)}U_g\xi$ is strongly continuous and compactly supported: near g the functions f(g,.) vary uniformly on a common compact base set. Its Bochner integral defines pi, with the displayed norm bound. Covariance gives $U_h M_b=M_{b\circ h^{-1}}U_h$, so expanding the product and applying Bochner/Fubini yields $\pi(f_1)\pi(f_2)=\int\!\int M_{f_1(h,x)f_2(r,h^{-1}x)}U_{hr}\,dh\,dr=\pi(f_1*f_2)$ after the left-Haar substitution g=hr. The adjoint identity follows from $U_g^*M_{\overline{f(g,\cdot)}}=M_{\overline{f(g,g\,\cdot)}}U_{g^{-1}}$ and Haar inversion, giving the stated modular involution. For nondegeneracy, choose $0\le b_n\le1$ in Cc(X) with b_n tending pointwise to 1, from a compact exhaustion and cutoff lemma; bounded PVM dominated convergence gives $M_{b_n}\to I$ strongly. Choose the published nonnegative norm-one group approximate identity a_i supported near e; strong continuity gives $U(a_i)\to I$. Then $\pi(a_i\otimes b_n)=M_{b_n}U(a_i)$ approximates every vector by first choosing n and then i. Thus the closed span of pi(Cc)H is H. The selected homogeneous-space case X=G/H satisfies every added topological hypothesis.

lem-the-imprimitivity-reconstruction-map.interface: Assume AC. In the normalized model of a transitive system $(U,P)$ on $G/H$, take the Borel unitaries B and the stabilizer representation sigma supplied by the preceding lemma. Multiplication by B is unitary and $$(B^{-1}WU_gW^{-1}Bf)(x)=D_g(x)^{1/2}\sigma(s(x)^{-1}gs(g^{-1}x))f(g^{-1}x).$$ This is the canonical induced action of $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\sigma$. Moreover $B^{-1}WP(E)W^{-1}B=M_{\mathbf1_E}$ for all Borel E. Hence $(U,P)$ is unitarily equivalent to the canonical induced system by an isometric map intertwining both U and P.
lem-the-imprimitivity-reconstruction-map.strategy: The preceding lemma supplies a Borel unitary B, so its multiplication operator is unitary. The source-variable convention is $WU_gW^{-1}f(x)=D_g(x)^{1/2}\varphi_g(g^{-1}x)f(g^{-1}x)$. Substitute $\varphi_g(g^{-1}x)=B_x\sigma(s(x)^{-1}gs(g^{-1}x))B_{g^{-1}x}^{-1}$ and conjugate by B. The B factors cancel at their respective target and source points, yielding exactly the displayed section form of the published covariant induced representation. Being decomposable, B commutes with scalar multiplication and therefore with all PVM indicators. The induction measure-independence theorem handles the equivalent finite representative. Thus the map is onto, isometric, and intertwines both members of the system.

thm-mackey-imprimitivity-theorem.interface: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff topological group, $H\le G$ a closed subgroup, and $(U,P)$ a transitive system of imprimitivity on $G/H$ acting on a separable Hilbert space $H_0$. Then there exist a strongly continuous unitary representation $\sigma:H\to U(K)$ on a separable Hilbert space $K$ and a unitary $$W:H_0\longrightarrow L^2(G/H,\mu;K)$$ onto the induced space of $\sigma$ such that $$WU_gW^{-1}=\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\sigma(g)\quad(g\in G),\qquad WP(E)W^{-1}=M_{\mathbf 1_E}\quad(E\subseteq G/H\ \text{Borel}),$$ where $M_{\mathbf 1_E}$ is multiplication by the indicator of $E$ on the covariant model. Conversely, for every strongly continuous unitary $\sigma:H\to U(K)$ the induced representation together with multiplication by indicators on $G/H$ is a transitive system of imprimitivity, and the two constructions are inverse up to unitary equivalence. The uniqueness theorem records the corresponding bijection of equivalence classes.
thm-mackey-imprimitivity-theorem.strategy: For the zero Hilbert space choose the zero stabilizer fibre and the zero induced system. For a nonzero system, the forward direction assembles the spectral multiplicity model, the cocycle fields and the reconstruction unitary: the model gives the base and the PVM action, the cocycle fields produce the stabilizer representation, and the reconstruction map conjugates the system into the canonical induced system. The reverse direction is the canonical-system lemma. Both directions use the second countability of $G$ through the Borel cross-section and the standard Borel structure of $G/H$, and the separability of the Hilbert spaces through the multiplicity model. No regularity of the PVM is needed once the measure model is fixed, and the statement makes no claim for nontransitive or non-standard orbit spaces.

thm-uniqueness-in-mackey-imprimitivity.interface: Assume AC and keep the hypotheses of the imprimitivity theorem. If $\sigma:H\to U(K)$ and $\sigma':H\to U(K')$ are strongly continuous unitary representations, then the canonical transitive systems of $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\sigma$ and $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\sigma'$ on $G/H$ are unitarily equivalent if and only if $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ are unitarily equivalent. Consequently the map of the imprimitivity theorem is a bijection between unitary equivalence classes of transitive systems on $G/H$ and unitary equivalence classes of strongly continuous unitary representations of $H$.
thm-uniqueness-in-mackey-imprimitivity.strategy: An H-intertwining unitary acts fibrewise and intertwines the canonical systems. Conversely a system equivalence intertwines scalar multiplications, so the published commutant and multiplicity-rigidity suppliers make it multiplication by a Borel unitary field A between equal-dimensional fibres. Fix a unitary identification of those fibres. The G-intertwining equation says the source cocycles for sigma and sigma-prime differ by the gauge A. Apply the Haar-Fubini uniqueness proof in the regularization lemma: lifting the gauge to G makes $b_2(t)^{-1}A(q(t))b_1(t)$ left-translation invariant for every g a.e., hence a constant unitary T. Right-H covariance gives $\sigma'(h)T=T\sigma(h)$ for every h. This proves equivalence of the stabilizer representations without evaluating A at a null coset. The two directions give the claimed bijection. Zero fibres induce exactly the zero system; a nonzero fibre induces a nonzero space by the full-support quotient measure and nonzero square-integrable sections, so the zero cases are immediate.

cor-mackey-little-group-reduction-for-an.interface: Assume AC. Let $G=N\rtimes K$ be a semidirect product with $N$ abelian and closed normal, $G$ second countable locally compact, and let the dual action of $K$ on $\widehat N$ have regular orbits in the sense of the preceding lemma (equivalently, the orbit space $\widehat N/K$ is countably separated). For $\chi\in\widehat N$ let $K_\chi=\{k\in K:k\cdot\chi=\chi\}$ and $H_\chi=N\rtimes K_\chi$. Then every irreducible strongly continuous unitary representation $\pi$ of $G$ is unitarily equivalent to $\operatorname{Ind}_{H_\chi}^G(\chi\otimes\theta)$ for some $\chi\in\widehat N$ and some irreducible strongly continuous unitary representation $\theta$ of $K_\chi$, where $\chi\otimes\theta$ denotes the representation $(n,k_\chi)\mapsto\chi(n)\theta(k_\chi)$ of $H_\chi$.
cor-mackey-little-group-reduction-for-an.strategy:
The proved local spectral lemma applied to pi restricted to N gives the covariant PVM on its dual. Irreducibility makes every invariant spectral projection zero or I, so the system is ergodic. The regular-orbit concentration lemma gives an orbit $C=K\cdot\chi$ with P(C)=I. The stabilizer Kchi is closed by continuity of the dual action. The orbit map $K/K_\chi\to C$ is continuous and injective. Its domain is second-countable LCH, hence admits a countable compact exhaustion; its restriction to each compact is a homeomorphism onto a compact subset of the Hausdorff dual. Both the full domain and every open subset are sigma-compact, so their images are countable unions of compact sets and thus Borel. This proves that C is Borel and the inverse orbit map is Borel. Also $G/(N\rtimes K_\chi)\cong K/K_\chi$. Transport the system and apply Mackey to obtain sigma of Hchi and an equivalence with its induced system.
To prove $\sigma|_N=\chi I$ rigorously, the original N action in this model is multiplication by the character at x: $\pi(n)f(x)=(s(x)\cdot\chi)(n)f(x)$. Gauge B commutes with this scalar action. Since N fixes every base point, the induced formula gives $\sigma(s(x)^{-1}ns(x))=(s(x)\cdot\chi)(n)I=\chi(s(x)^{-1}ns(x))I$ almost everywhere x for each n. Take a countable dense subset of N, intersect its conull sets, and choose any x in that intersection. Strong continuity extends the equality to all n; conjugation by s(x) maps N onto itself, so $\sigma(m)=\chi(m)I$ for every m in N. This uses an actual conull point, not the null identity coset. Restrict sigma to Kchi to get a strongly continuous theta, and semidirect multiplication gives $\sigma(n,k)=\chi(n)\theta(k)$. Any nontrivial invariant subspace of theta splits sigma; its induced orthogonal splitting is nontrivial because the base measure has full support and each nonzero fibre yields nonzero square-integrable sections. This would split pi, hence theta is irreducible. The orbit is determined by the spectral PVM; the inducing class is determined by system uniqueness.

ex-imprimitivity-for-a-finite-transitive.interface: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a finite group acting transitively on a finite set $X$, fix $x_0\in X$, put $H=\operatorname{Stab}_G(x_0)$ and identify $X$ with $G/H$. Let $\mathcal H=\ell^2(X)$ carry the permutation representation $U$, and let $P$ be the projection-valued measure on $X$ assigning to $E\subseteq X$ the orthogonal projection onto the coordinate subspace $\ell^2(E)$. Then $(U,P)$ is a transitive system of imprimitivity on the finite standard Borel space $X$, and it is unitarily equivalent to the canonical system of the trivial representation $1_H$ of $H$; the induced representation $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G1_H$ is the permutation representation on $G/H$, so the finite case of Mackey's theorem reduces to the classical stabilizer/induction classification. More generally a finite-dimensional unitary representation of $G$ carrying a transitive system on $X$ is induced from a unitary representation of $H$ on a fibre of dimension $\dim(\mathcal H)/|X|$, by the general theorem.
ex-imprimitivity-for-a-finite-transitive.strategy: The permutation representation is unitary and finite-dimensional, hence strongly continuous, and the orthogonal coordinate projections satisfy $UP(E)U^{-1}=P(gE)$ by equivariance of the permutation action. The identification with the induced system is the general Mackey theorem; independently, the published finite-group computation identifies $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G1_H$ with the permutation representation on $G/H$. The finite set $X$ is standard Borel as a countable discrete space. The cited general theorem supplies the inducing representation under AC; in the permutation case it is the trivial representation. For the final clause, the mutually orthogonal fibres $P(\{x\})\mathcal H$ all have equal dimension because U transports them transitively, and their direct sum is the full representation space. Thus the stabilizer fibre has dimension $\dim(\mathcal H)/|X|$; the induced representation has the original total dimension. AC is inherited precisely when the general Mackey theorem identifies the system with an induced system and classifies the arbitrary finite-dimensional system in the final clause. The displayed finite permutation and equal-fibre-dimension calculations themselves use only finite choices. The finite base has the explicit discrete metric d(x,y)=0 for x=y and 1 otherwise. Its full finite set is dense, every Cauchy sequence is eventually constant, and every subset is open; hence it is Polish and its full power-set sigma-algebra is standard Borel by the definitions. No standard-Borel example with an AI-generated statement is used as a proof supplier.

ex-little-groups-for-the-real-ax-plus-b-.interface: Assume AC. Let $G=\operatorname{Aff}(\mathbb R)=\mathbb R\rtimes\mathbb R^\times$, N its translation subgroup, and K its dilation subgroup. Identify $\widehat N\cong\mathbb R$ by $\chi_\lambda(x)=e^{i\lambda x}$. The dual action is $\lambda\mapsto\lambda/k$, so the full group K has two orbits, $\{0\}$ and $\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, with stabilizers K and $\{1\}$ respectively. Its little groups are G and N. The irreducible representations are the one-dimensional characters $|a|^{it}\operatorname{sign}(a)^\delta$ for $t\in\mathbb R$, $\delta\in\{0,1\}$, and one infinite-dimensional class $\pi=\operatorname{Ind}_N^G\chi_1\cong\operatorname{Ind}_N^G\chi_{-1}$. For the orientation-preserving group $G_0=\mathbb R\rtimes\mathbb R_{>0}$ the nonzero dual orbits are separately $(0,\infty)$ and $(-\infty,0)$; they give two inequivalent infinite-dimensional representations $\pi_1,\pi_{-1}$, alongside the characters $a^{it}$. Thus $\widehat G=(\mathbb R\times\{0,1\})\sqcup\{\pi\}$ and $\widehat{G_0}=\mathbb R\sqcup\{\pi_1,\pi_{-1}\}$.
ex-little-groups-for-the-real-ax-plus-b-.strategy:
Compute $(k\cdot\chi_\lambda)(x)=\chi_\lambda(x/k)$, hence parameter $\lambda/k$. Negative dilations join the two signs in the full group, while positive dilations preserve them. The resulting finite orbit partitions are regular, so the proved little-group corollary makes the stated inductions and quotient characters exhaustive. Every irreducible representation of the abelian quotient K is one-dimensional by the published unitary Schur lemma. Logarithm identifies its positive subgroup with the additive real line, whose characters are $e^{it\log a}$; the order-two sign subgroup gives $\operatorname{sign}(a)^\delta$.
For a nonzero character the inducing fibre is one-dimensional. In its canonical system, N acts by multiplication by the point of the nonzero dual orbit; pushing the canonical PVM to that orbit gives its spectral PVM by the proved spectral-uniqueness lemma. Any operator commuting with the induced representation therefore commutes with that PVM (integrate against L1, use the dense Fourier C0 algebra and regular-PVM uniqueness), hence is multiplication by a bounded scalar function by the diagonal commutant theorem. Commutation with the whole group makes that function invariant almost everywhere under the transitive quotient action; the proved ergodicity lemma applied to rational superlevel sets of its real and imaginary parts makes it constant. The induced representation is thus irreducible by the unitary Schur criterion. Conjugating the induction datum by a dilation provides a unitary equivalence for parameters in the same orbit: translation of the covariant functions by that dilation intertwines, with the positive square-root measure factor from induction measure independence. For opposite signs in G0 the spectral supports are disjoint, so spectral uniqueness prohibits equivalence. The nonzero orbits carry nonatomic full-support measures and infinitely many disjoint positive-measure sets, so their L2 spaces are infinite-dimensional. These computations establish the source classification, rather than merely citing it. AC is inherited in the exhaustiveness claim through the little-group corollary, in the spectral-PVM and diagonal-commutant proof of irreducibility, and in the induced-model and measure-independence suppliers. The direct dual-orbit calculation itself requires no choice beyond finite selections.

ex-the-regular-position-momentum-imprimi.interface: Assume AC. Let $G=\mathbb R^n$ act on $X=\mathbb R^n$ by translation, let $U=\lambda_G$ be the left regular representation on $L^2(\mathbb R^n)$, and let $P(E)$ be multiplication by the indicator of a Borel set $E\subseteq\mathbb R^n$. Then $(U,P)$ is a transitive system of imprimitivity on $\mathbb R^n=\mathbb R^n/\{0\}$ with trivial stabilizer, $P$ is the joint spectral measure of the $n$ commuting self-adjoint position operators $M_{x_j}$ of multiplication by the coordinates, and $U$ is the representation induced from the trivial representation of the trivial subgroup; the generators of the one-parameter groups $t\mapsto U_{te_j}$ are the momentum operators $-i\partial_j$. The system is the classical model behind the imprimitivity theorem and behind the position-momentum form of the Stone-von Neumann uniqueness theorem.
ex-the-regular-position-momentum-imprimi.strategy: Compute $U_tP(E)U_t^{-1}=P(t+E)$ directly from $(U_tf)(x)=f(x-t)$, verify the PVM axioms for multiplication by indicators, and identify the stabilizer of the origin as trivial. The identity $U=\operatorname{Ind}_{\{0\}}^{\mathbb R^n}1$ is the $H=\{e\}$ clause of the published induction theorem, and the position operators are multiplication by the coordinate functions, whose joint spectral measure is $P$. The momentum identification is the published one-parameter group generated by the coordinate translations; no Heisenberg commutation relation on a common invariant domain is asserted. AC is inherited through the published unitary-induction and canonical-system suppliers used to identify the model and its induced representation. The indicator covariance computation is direct; the full example retains the choice hypothesis of its analytical suppliers. For the standard-Borel assertion use the explicit finite-dimensional metric d_infty(x,y)=max_j|x_j-y_j|. A Cauchy sequence converges coordinatewise by real completeness and then in this maximum metric. The finite product Q^n is countable and dense by the published rational/countable-product suppliers, so R^n is Polish and its Borel measurable space is standard Borel by definition; n=0 is the singleton case. This direct argument replaces the prohibited AI-generated example dependency.

def-transitive-system-of-imprimitivity.interface: A system of imprimitivity $(U,P)$ on a standard Borel $G$-space $X$ is **transitive** when $X$ is $G$-equivariantly isomorphic to a homogeneous space $G/H$ with $H\le G$ closed, the isomorphism carrying the Borel structure of $G/H$ (hence then $G$ is second-countable locally compact, the action on $G/H$ is the left-coset action, and the stabilizer of the identity coset is $H$). For a transitive system one fixes the base identification $X=G/H$. Assume AC for the following normalized-measure existence and uniqueness assertions: a **normalized representative** is a strongly quasi-invariant Radon measure $\mu_\rho$ on $G/H$ built from a rho-function $\rho$. The normalized homogeneous measure class is the unique class of nonzero quasi-invariant Radon measures on $G/H$; the system is called transitive on $G/H$.
def-transitive-system-of-imprimitivity.strategy: The equivariant Borel coset-space condition defines transitivity without invoking choice or a classification theorem. AC is needed for the asserted normalized-measure supply: existence is the published rho-function theorem, and uniqueness of the nonzero sigma-finite quasi-invariant class is the proved local Haar-lift lemma, not an unstated uniqueness clause of the existence theorem. Different rho-functions give representatives in this class. The identity-coset stabilizer is H by the explicit coset computation. Consumers that use only the definitional term transitive do not consume the normalized-measure existence assertion.

cex-a-nontransitive-system-is-not-classi.interface: Let $G=\mathbb Z/2=\{e,s\}$, let $X=\{a,b,c\}$ with $s\cdot a=a$ and $s\cdot b=c$, and let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^3$ with the direct sum of the trivial representation on $\mathbb C\delta_a$ and the regular representation on $\mathbb C\delta_b\oplus\mathbb C\delta_c$; let $P$ be the projection-valued measure with $P(\{a\}),P(\{b\}),P(\{c\})$ the three coordinate projections. Then $(U,P)$ is a system of imprimitivity on the standard Borel space $X$; the two orbits are $\{a\}$ and $\{b,c\}$, the projections $P(\{a\})$ and $P(\{b,c\})$ are nontrivial and invariant, and the system is not transitive (nor ergodic). No closed subgroup $H\le G$ with a strongly continuous unitary representation $\sigma$ classifies it: every homogeneous space $G/H$ has one or two points, so it cannot be equivariantly identified with the three-point base, and the theorem correctly decomposes the system as the direct sum of the transitive systems on the two orbits. Hence transitivity (or ergodicity) is essential to the one-subgroup form of Mackey's imprimitivity theorem.
cex-a-nontransitive-system-is-not-classi.strategy: Verify the covariance relation on the three coordinate projections: $s$ fixes $\delta_a$ and swaps $\delta_b,\delta_c$, so $UP(\{b\})U^{-1}=P(\{c\})=P(s\{b\})$ and $UP(\{a\})U^{-1}=P(\{a\})$. The nontrivial invariant projection $P(\{a\})$ witnesses failure of ergodicity and transitivity (a transitive system on a homogeneous space has P concentrated on a single orbit). For the non-classification: $G$ has exactly two coset spaces up to equivariant Borel isomorphism (the point and the two-point free orbit), and neither is the three-point $X$; the classification by one subgroup therefore cannot hold, while the system splits over the orbit partition into the transitive pieces $G/G$ on $\{a\}$ and $G/\{e\}$ on $\{b,c\}$. This is a choice-free finite construction: all projections, group actions, orbit decompositions and coset cardinalities are computed explicitly. The general Mackey theorem is only the comparison statement; its AC-dependent classification is not used to establish this counterexample. The finite base has the explicit discrete metric d(x,y)=0 for x=y and 1 otherwise. Its full finite set is dense, every Cauchy sequence is eventually constant, and every subset is open; hence it is Polish and its full power-set sigma-algebra is standard Borel by the definitions. No standard-Borel example with an AI-generated statement is used as a proof supplier.
